pr_body:
The EGL stuff is really complicated because of historical reasons
(tl;dr: blame EGL). There was one edge case with EGL context creation
that lead to incorrect behavior. EGL_KHR_create_context was created with
EGL 1.4 (which mpv does support) but it is still possible for an EGL 1.4
device to not implement this extension. That means that none of the EGL
attrs that pass a specific opengl version work. So for this obscure
case, there is a fallback context creation at the very end which simply
creates an EGLContext without passing any special attrs.

This has another problem however. mpv has a hard requirement on at least
desktop opengl 2.1 or opengl ES 2.0 to function (we're not asking for
much here). Since the fallback EGL context creation has no version
checking, it is entirely possible to create an EGL context with a
desktop opengl version under 2.1. As you get further along in the code,
the user will encounter the hard opengl version check and then error
out. However, we're supposed to also actually check if GLES works
(that's what the opengl-es=auto option is for) so this is a bug.

The fix is to do a bit of code duplication and make a mpgl_check_version
specifically for if we hit the edge case of needing to create an EGL
context without the EGL_KHR_create_context extension. Grab the version
with the function pointer, check if it's under 210, if so destroy the
EGL context and set it to NULL. After that, if the user has set
opengl-es to auto, mpv will try GLES next. If it is set to no, then mpv
will simply fail as desired. Fixes #5915.

Sidenote: the ra_gl_ctx_test_version originally testing 140 doesn't make
any sense. Passing the version number in that function only does
something if the user has set opengl-restrict. What we need to do is to
pass the version of the created context to that function. If the version
is higher than the opengl-restrict option, then make this a failure.
pr_comments:
Note that despite the suggestion, the commit itself is correct and should fix the mentioned bug.

Albeit the GLES handling should be simplified by constructing appropriate `es[]` array in `mpegl_create_context_cb()` and removing the GLES checking from `ra_gl_ctx_test_version()`... Bth this is just an idea.

issue_context.title: --opengl-es=auto does not attempt to use OpenGL ES
issue_context.body:
Somewhat related to #5903 

### mpv version and platform

mpv 0.28.2
Arch Linux x86_64

```
mpv 0.28.2 (C) 2000-2017 mpv/MPlayer/mplayer2 projects
 built on Mon May 14 09:49:30 CEST 2018
ffmpeg library versions:
   libavutil       56.14.100
   libavcodec      58.18.100
   libavformat     58.12.100
   libswscale      5.1.100
   libavfilter     7.16.100
   libswresample   3.1.100
ffmpeg version: 4.0
```

### Reproduction steps

Have an old computer which supports only really old OpenGL versions (in my case, OpenGL 1.4 and OpenGL ES 2.0)
**OR**
(if you use mesa) Use the `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE` and `MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE` environment variables to change reported OpenGL(ES) versions
**THEN**
Play videos with `--vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=(yes/no/auto)`

### Expected behavior

When video is played with `--opengl-es=auto`, mpv detects the system's OpenGL and OpenGL ES versions, and makes a decision whether to use one or the other based on the versions. (e.g. if OpenGL <2.1 but OpenGL ES =2.0, OpenGL ES is selected)

When video is played with `--opengl-es=(yes/no)`, then OpenGL ES is forced or disabled appropriately.

### Actual behavior

When `--opengl-es=auto` is used and OpenGL is _available_ (not necessarily usable), then mpv only tries to use it, and errors when the OpenGL version is insufficient. No attempt is made to use OpenGL ES.

When `--opengl-es=yes` is used and OpenGL (not ES) is _usable_, then OpenGL is used, not OpenGL ES.

### Log file

`mpv --vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=auto` https://0x0.st/s_U0.txt

In this one I use environment variables to force mesa to accept OpenGL 2.1 contexts, even if they aren't supported by the hardware, and to reject OpenGL ES contexts newer than 1.0.
`MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=2.1 MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=1.0 mpv --vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=yes` https://0x0.st/s_Uk.txt

### Sample files

Happens with every file I tried so far, so I'm fairly sure I don't need to upload samples.

The `--opengl-es=auto` behaviour is still the same either side of the commit. This might not be a bug, but it's unintuitive and imo needs to be explicitly stated in the documentation.

Thanks for reminding me about this three-year-old issue! I tested just now with mpv 0.33.1 and the issue mostly no longer occurs, in that setting `--opengl-es=yes` and `--opengl-es=no` correctly force on or force off the use of OpenGL ES. However, `--opengl-es=auto` still behaves as described in the issue, and doesn't attempt to use OpenGL ES.

To clarify, the testing method I'm using is as follows:
```
$ MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=1.0 MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=1.0 mpv --vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=auto media/video/sleetcat.mp4
# this fails, as expected
$ MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=2.1 MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=1.0 mpv --vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=auto media/video/sleetcat.mp4
# this works and uses OpenGL, as expected
$ MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=1.0 MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=2.0 mpv --vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=auto media/video/sleetcat.mp4
# this fails. i expect it to attempt OpenGL ES
$ MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=2.1 MESA_GLES_VERSION_OVERRIDE=2.0 mpv --vo=gpu --gpu-api=opengl --opengl-es=auto media/video/sleetcat.mp4
# this works and uses OpenGL, as expected
```
in particular, i expect the third case to work because, if i select `--opengl-es=yes`, the video plays perfectly fine

Okay yeah that makes sense. The third case does sound like a legitimate bug with `--opengl-es=auto` option. It should make an attempt to use GLES if Desktop Opengl fails for some reason (otherwise what's the point of having an auto option).

Okay so I figured out why this occurs. This behavior will only happen if you use `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE` or some other thing that tricks `glGetString` into reporting a value that is less than 210. mpv has a hard requirement on at least 210 or 200 (for es). In the common opengl code, this is checked using glGetString. Thus, you get a a fatal error and mpv quits. However, the only reason the code reaches that far in the first place is because the check in EGL is passed when the EGLContext is created (i.e. you are able to create a valid EGL context because your drivers support it). mpv just loops through a hardcoded list of versions to try and you will successfully create a 4.4 context (or whatever it may be in your case).

On an actual device that doesn't actually support an appropriate desktop GL version, the `auto` behavior will work correctly (you can simulate this by simply always returning `false` in `create_context` in the desktop opengl portion). You will fail at creating any EGLContexts and then it will attempt with GLES later which will work (or maybe still fail if this device is that bad).

So I guess the actual bug here is that sometimes mpv cares about `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE` (when using `glGetString` even though it's implicit) and other times it totally ignores it (when probing contexts). It would be relatively simply to just parse that environment variable and take that into account but that's always a little icky. Not sure.

Thanks for the insight. I went ahead and tested on a real device which doesn't support OpenGL 2.1, but does support OpenGL ES 2.0, and I still get the behaviour I found before.

https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/799722753325400095/868191893568258118/mpvlognv.txt

(These are discord uploads because the 0x0.st uploads didn't survive the age of this issue)

That's a very interesting result. I'd expect `eglCreateContext` to fail if you try to create an EGLContext for an OpenGL version that is not supported. If I simulate this with the `MESA_GL_VERSION_OVERRIDE=2.1` environment variable, that's what happens. It cycles through the loop and fails until `210` is tried. Apparently, that doesn't happen on your device for some reason. I don't know why that would be the case.

I found the code you mentioned, that tries a hardcoded list of OpenGL versions.

https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/blob/master/video/out/opengl/egl_helpers.c#L191-L196

However, there's an additional check for EGL version 1.4, which causes the code to ignore the hardcoded list of versions, and proceed with whatever it gets.

Oh duh, how did I miss that. ~~At least on the surface, that looks like something that shouldn't exist~~. I'll run through the git history.

Edit: Okay, probably some extra check should be performed on that ctx before we proceed onward.

 - kill off the unused ctx argument

   - Mali drivers on EGL 1.4 expose GL API statically from
